system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
| Issue | Seller’s position | What Buyer should want | Recommendation / reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **20% of price (AUD 4.8m)**. | A materially higher general cap, ideally **100% of price**, or a risk-based cap supported by diligence. | **Reject; seek a higher cap.** A 20% cap may leave the Buyer substantially under-protected for breaches affecting the value of the acquired business. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 de minimis and AUD 250,000 tipping point, but only the excess above the basket is recoverable. | A lower de minimis and a **tipping basket** once crossed, so all qualifying losses are recoverable; exclude specified claims from thresholds. | **Counter with a lower, tipping basket and appropriate exclusions.** The proposed deductible basket makes the Buyer absorb the first AUD 250,000 as well as smaller claims. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | General Warranty Claims notified within **18 months**; Seller also proposes applying any limitation to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise. | A longer period for general warranties and distinct, longer or statutory periods for tax, title, fundamental and indemnity claims; clear claim-notification and proceedings rules. | **Reject the blanket approach; negotiate category-specific periods.** Eighteen months may be too short, and a general limit should not silently truncate other claims. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties subject to the general cap and time limits. | Separate, materially higher or uncapped protection for capacity, authority and title, with longer claim periods. | **Reject; carve fundamental and title claims out of the general regime.** Defects in the Seller’s authority or ownership threaten the transaction itself. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims; no express fraud carve-out is stated. | Expressly disapply caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance restrictions to fraud and fraudulent misrepresentation, subject to applicable law. | **Require an express fraud carve-out.** The Seller should not obtain contractual protection for its own fraud. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | Broad general disclosure of the data room (DD-002–DD-012), Accounts, statutory registers and public records, plus specific disclosures. | Specific, fair disclosure against each relevant warranty, with sufficient detail for the Buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter; no blanket data-room or public-register disclosure. | **Reject general disclosure; retain only sufficiently specific disclosures.** A blanket incorporation makes it difficult to know which facts qualify which warranties. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known by Buyer or its advisers, including matters discoverable in the data room or public records. | No broad imputed or constructive-knowledge bar; at most, tightly defined actual knowledge of named deal personnel, without limiting fraud or express indemnities. | **Reject as drafted.** “Discoverable” knowledge converts access to information into a broad waiver of warranty protection. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Seller to use reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of counterparty written consent. DD-002 indicates about AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue (~30%) and consent conditions; final consent and evidence conditions are absent. | A condition to Completion requiring valid written consent **and satisfaction or waiver of all clause 11.3 conditions**; no deemed satisfaction merely on delivery. | **Make consent and its conditions a condition precedent, with no completion until evidenced.** Bluefen’s revenue concentration makes an ineffective or conditional consent a material continuity risk. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | Approximately AUD 3.2m outstanding; release to follow Completion. Disclosure says it remains unpaid and no final discharge is included. | Repayment at or before Completion from agreed funds flow, with lender payoff evidence and effective release/discharge of all security as a completion deliverable. | **Do not accept a post-Completion release promise.** The Buyer should not inherit debt or encumbered assets after paying the price. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | DD-005 bonuses of AUD 420,000 are not separately itemised in funds flow; tax, superannuation and on-cost treatment is unstated. | Quantify gross liabilities and on-costs; settle or deduct them at Completion under agreed debt/transaction-expense or price mechanics, with supporting funds-flow detail. | **Require full quantification and explicit funds-flow treatment before signing/completion.** Otherwise the Buyer risks paying the price while inheriting undisclosed completion-triggered liabilities. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Existing indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; Seller considers it adequate. DD-004 says transfer depends on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee; DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open, without independent proof of non-payment, and no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment is disclosed. | Effective transfer/assignment of all relevant Project Materials at or before Completion, supported by evidence; a specific indemnity for loss, claims, costs and remediation arising from failure of title/transfer, not merely the payment amount. | **Expand the indemnity and make effective transfer a completion deliverable.** The disclosed record leaves both payment status and ownership/assignment unverified. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | DD-006 characterised as preliminary and not expected to be material; scope, access and notification position remain unresolved. | Complete investigation and scope assessment, preserve evidence, assess notification/remediation obligations, and obtain a tailored indemnity for incident-related claims, costs and remediation; consider a specific completion condition if unresolved. | **Do not accept a materiality dismissal; seek a specific risk allocation and verified incident status.** The disclosed data set and unknown access create unresolved privacy and response-cost exposure. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three renewals totalling AUD 330,000 described as ordinary-course operating costs. DD-008 and DD-011 should be read together; avoidability, termination, accrual and ordinary-course status are unstated. | Reconcile timing and scope, verify commitments and termination rights, and reflect accrued or unpaid amounts in the agreed price/debt-like mechanics; obtain consent if required by the SPA. | **Require a documented reconciliation and explicit price treatment.** Calling them ordinary-course does not establish whether they create incremental or unavoidable liabilities. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | Seller says limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims; tax and IP are said to be settled under the general regime. | Separate and expressly define general warranty, fundamental/title, tax, specific indemnity, fraud and other claims, with tailored caps, baskets, time limits and remedies. | **Reject “all Claims” treatment; create express category carve-outs.** Different risks need different protection, and the Seller’s language could unintentionally apply general limits across the board. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | Seller relies on DD-012 share register recording it as holder of 100% of issued shares. | Independently verify the register, issued capital, encumbrances and transfer mechanics; require title warranties, executed transfer documents and delivery of share certificates or appropriate replacement evidence. | **Do not treat the register alone as conclusive verification.** The disclosure identifies its source but expressly does not establish Buyer verification. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Seller considers tax and IP positions settled under the general regime, without separate terms in the materials provided. | Obtain express tax and IP warranty/indemnity terms, tailored caps and survival periods, and confirm treatment of pre-Completion tax and IP ownership/chain-of-title risks. | **Keep these terms open pending agreed drafting and diligence.** The Seller’s assertion does not resolve the distinct exposure or supply operative protections. |

These are buyer-side negotiation recommendations based on the supplied Seller materials, not a review of the full SPA or a substitute for advice on the complete transaction documents.
=== END ADVICE ===
